note: Attacker-controlled bytes are written verbatim to a .pcap file; the file contains a single Ethernet frame with an IPv4/GRE packet whose GRE payload is exactly 4 bytes.
The pcap reader parses the file and produces a RawPacket containing the 38-byte frame (14-byte Ethernet + 20-byte IPv4 + 4-byte GRE).
Packet parsing walks the layer chain: EthLayer creates IPv4Layer, which sees IP protocol 47 (GRE).
payloadLen is 4 (the GRE payload). getGREVersion checks greDataLen >= sizeof(gre_basic_header) (4) and returns GREv0 because the version field is 0.

code: m_NextLayer = new GREv0Layer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet)
note: A GREv0Layer is constructed with m_Data pointing to the 4-byte GRE buffer and m_DataLen = 4. The GRE header has checksumBit=1 (byte 0 bit 0) and version=0.
Packet::computeCalculateFields iterates from the last layer upward, calling each layer's computeCalculateFields; GREv0Layer::computeCalculateFields is invoked.
checksumBit is 1, so the function proceeds to compute and write the GRE checksum.
setChecksum is called with 0; inside setChecksum, needToExtendLayer is false because checksumBit==1, so no layer extension occurs.

code: uint8_t* offsetPtr = getFieldValue(GreChecksumOrRouting, true); int offset = offsetPtr - m_Data;
note: getFieldValue returns m_Data + 4 (the checksum/routing field position), so offset = 4.
Writes 2 bytes at m_Data + 4. Since m_DataLen is only 4, this is a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 2 past the end of the GRE buffer.
